lead: Digital passband modulation puts bits onto a radio carrier and gets them back: ASK, FSK, BPSK, DPSK, QPSK, M-ary PSK, M-ary FSK, QAM, MSK and GMSK, then spread spectrum and OFDM. After it you can draw each modulator and receiver, compute symbol rates, bandwidths and error probabilities, compare spectra, and choose a scheme for a given power, bandwidth and channel.
about: The unit moves from the simplest binary schemes to the systems inside today's radios. ASK and FSK come first, then BPSK, the reference for every error-rate comparison, and the non-coherent receivers (envelope FSK and DPSK) that do without a carrier phase. QPSK and M-ary PSK add bits per symbol on a circle; M-ary FSK and QAM trade bandwidth against power in opposite directions; MSK and GMSK keep a constant envelope with a compact spectrum. The constellation chapter ties these together by distance, bandwidth efficiency and power spectral density. Spread spectrum and OFDM close the unit: one spreads the signal to beat interference, the other splits it into many slow subcarriers to beat multipath fading. The correlator receiver and signal space from baseband data transmission are used throughout.

chapters.idea: Map each bit to a carrier amplitude (ASK) or one of two carrier frequencies (FSK), then recover it with a matched-filter or correlator receiver.
chapters.depth: Cover binary ASK, also called on-off keying (OOK): s(t)=A b(t) cos(2πf_c t), where b(t) is 0 or 1, A is carrier amplitude and f_c is carrier frequency. Show generation by multiplier or switch. Cover coherent detection: multiply by a local carrier, integrate over the bit, compare with a threshold. Cover binary FSK (BFSK): two tones at f_0 and f_1, generation by voltage-controlled oscillator or switched oscillators, coherent detection by two correlators. Define modulation index h=2Δf/R_b, where Δf is frequency deviation and R_b is bit rate. Give null-to-null bandwidth 2R_b for ASK and Carson bandwidth 2(Δf+R_b) for BFSK. State coherent orthogonality spacing 1/(2T_b) and noncoherent spacing 1/T_b, where T_b is bit duration. Sketch PSD qualitatively. Give P_b=Q(√(E_b/N0)) for coherent BFSK and OOK, where E_b is bit energy, N0 is noise power spectral density, and Q(x) is the Gaussian tail probability. Keep error analysis to one formula each.

figure.title: ASK and FSK: generation and coherent detection
figure.aria: Binary data branches to an ASK multiplier and an FSK switch, then passes through a channel and a coherent detector to output bits.

chapters.example: A binary FSK transmitter sends 10 kbps. The mark frequency is 100 kHz and the space frequency is 110 kHz. Find the frequency deviation Δf, modulation index h, Carson bandwidth, and the minimum coherent tone spacing for orthogonality. Answer: Δf=(110−100)/2=5 kHz. h=2Δf/R_b=(2×5 kHz)/(10 kbps)=1. Carson bandwidth B=2(Δf+R_b)=2(5+10) kHz=30 kHz. Minimum coherent spacing is 1/(2T_b)=R_b/2=5 kHz. The actual spacing is 10 kHz, so the tones are orthogonal.
chapters.trap: Using R_b in place of T_b in the bandwidth formula, or forgetting that BFSK has two tones and needs a minimum spacing. For equiprobable OOK bits, average power is half the peak power.
chapters.prereq: Unit 1 complex envelope and AWGN; Unit 5 matched filter and signal space.
chapters.leave: Noncoherent envelope detection and DPSK to 6.3; BPSK error analysis to 6.2; constellation comparisons to 6.7.

chapters.idea: Send one bit as two opposite carrier phases; antipodal signalling gives the best binary error probability in AWGN.
chapters.depth: Cover BPSK waveform s(t)=±√(2E_b/T_b) cos(2πf_c t), where E_b is bit energy, T_b is bit duration and f_c is carrier frequency. Show generation by bipolar NRZ data multiplied by the carrier, also called a balanced modulator. Show coherent detection: multiply by a local carrier, integrate over one bit, decide at threshold zero. Draw the two-point constellation and the decision half-plane. Give P_b=Q(√(2E_b/N0))=½ erfc(√(E_b/N0)). Define Q(x) and erfc(x). State null-to-null bandwidth 2R_b and spectral efficiency 0.5 bps/Hz for rectangular pulses. Some syllabi call BPSK phase reversal keying (PRK). Compare briefly with coherent BFSK: BPSK has a 3 dB energy advantage for the same P_b.

figure.title: BPSK transmitter and coherent receiver
figure.aria: Bipolar data multiplies a carrier, crosses a channel, multiplies a local carrier, integrates, and passes a zero threshold to output bits.

chapters.example: A BPSK system sends 1 Mbps. The received Eb/N0 is 10 dB. Find the bit error probability and the expected number of errors in 10⁸ bits. Answer: Eb/N0=10 (10 dB). P_b=Q(√(2×10))=Q(√20)=Q(4.47)≈3.9×10⁻⁶. Expected errors =10⁸×3.9×10⁻⁶≈390 bits.
chapters.trap: Forgetting the factor 2 in Q(√(2E_b/N0)). Do not use E_s in place of E_b for BPSK. BPSK and Gray-coded QPSK have the same P_b for the same E_b, but their symbol error probabilities differ.
chapters.prereq: Unit 5 matched filter, signal space and AWGN error analysis; 6.1 for binary passband signals.
chapters.leave: QPSK and M-ary PSK to 6.4; noncoherent detection to 6.3; general constellation geometry to 6.7.

chapters.idea: When carrier phase is unknown, detect FSK by envelope or encode information in phase changes (DPSK), avoiding absolute phase recovery.
chapters.depth: Cover noncoherent BFSK: two bandpass filters followed by envelope detectors, then compare outputs. Give orthogonal tone spacing 1/T_b and P_b=½ exp(−E_b/(2N0)). Cover noncoherent OOK envelope detection with the same error form. Cover DPSK: differential encoder d_k=b_k⊕d_{k−1}, where b_k is the input bit, d_k is the encoded bit and ⊕ is XOR. Generation by phase changes of 180° for bit 1 and 0° for bit 0, or the opposite convention. Detection by multiplying the received signal with a one-bit delayed copy, lowpass filtering, and deciding. Give P_b≈½ exp(−E_b/N0). State that DPSK is slightly worse than coherent BPSK at the same E_b/N0. Some syllabi call DPSK differential phase shift keying. Keep phase-noise analysis qualitative.

figure.title: DPSK transmitter and delay detector
figure.aria: Data is differentially encoded, modulated, sent through a channel, split into a direct path and a one-bit delay, multiplied, lowpass filtered and thresholded.

chapters.example: A DPSK system uses the rule d_k=b_k⊕d_{k−1} with initial d_0=0. The bit stream is 1 1 0 1. Find the encoded bits d_k and the phase changes if bit 1 gives 180° and bit 0 gives 0°. Answer: d_1=1⊕0=1; d_2=1⊕1=0; d_3=0⊕0=0; d_4=1⊕0=1. Encoded bits d=1 0 0 1. Phase changes follow b: 180°, 180°, 0°, 180°. Decoding is b_k=d_k⊕d_{k−1}.
chapters.trap: Forgetting the initial reference bit in differential encoding. Do not use the coherent BPSK formula for DPSK. Noncoherent BFSK needs tone spacing 1/T_b, not 1/(2T_b).
chapters.prereq: 6.1 BFSK; 6.2 BPSK; Unit 5 matched filter and decision regions.
chapters.leave: Coherent BPSK to 6.2; M-ary noncoherent schemes to 6.5; fading effects to 6.9.

chapters.idea: Transmit two bits per symbol by choosing one of four phases (QPSK), and more bits by using M phases (M-ary PSK), trading noise margin for bandwidth.
chapters.depth: Cover QPSK as two BPSK signals on quadrature carriers: I and Q branches, each carrying one bit. Show generation by splitting the bit stream, converting to bipolar NRZ, multiplying by cos(2πf_c t) and sin(2πf_c t), then summing. Show coherent detection by two correlators, deciding I and Q, then mapping Gray labels. Give P_b=Q(√(2E_b/N0)) for Gray-coded QPSK, same as BPSK at the same E_b. Give general M-ary PSK: M=2^k, symbol rate R_s=R_b/k, null-to-null bandwidth 2R_s, bandwidth efficiency k/2 bps/Hz for rectangular pulses. Give P_s≈2Q(√(2E_s/N0) sin(π/M)) and P_b≈P_s/k, where E_s is symbol energy. Some syllabi call QPSK 4-PSK. Keep offset QPSK as a pointer to 6.6.

figure.aria: Four QPSK points at the corners of a square with Gray labels 00, 01, 11, 10; dashed edges join neighbours that differ in one bit.

chapters.example: A QPSK system sends 10 Mbps. Find the symbol rate, null-to-null bandwidth for rectangular pulses, bandwidth efficiency, and P_b when Eb/N0=10 dB. Answer: R_s=R_b/2=5 Msym/s. Null-to-null bandwidth B=2R_s=10 MHz. Bandwidth efficiency=10 Mbps/10 MHz=1 bps/Hz. P_b=Q(√(2×10))=Q(√20)≈3.9×10⁻⁶.
chapters.trap: Confusing bit rate R_b with symbol rate R_s. Do not put E_s into the BPSK formula when E_b is meant. Gray mapping lowers bit errors but does not change symbol error probability.
chapters.prereq: 6.2 BPSK; Unit 5 signal space and matched filter.
chapters.leave: M-ary FSK and QAM to 6.5; MSK and OQPSK to 6.6; constellation comparison to 6.7.

chapters.idea: Raise bits per symbol either with M orthogonal tones (MFSK) or with combined amplitude and phase levels (QAM), trading bandwidth against power.
chapters.depth: Cover M-ary FSK: M=2^k orthogonal tones, symbol rate R_s=R_b/k, coherent detection by a bank of M matched filters. Give elementary union-bound error form only; MFSK bandwidth grows roughly as M R_s. Cover QAM: M=4,16,64 square constellations, I and Q multilevel PAM. Show generation by two balanced modulators and a sum. Show coherent detection by two correlators with multilevel thresholds. Give P_s≈4(1−1/√M)Q(√(3E_s/((M−1)N0))) for square QAM, P_b≈P_s/log2 M, and bandwidth efficiency k/2 bps/Hz for rectangular pulses. Some syllabi call QAM quadrature amplitude modulation. Compare MFSK and QAM: MFSK needs more bandwidth, QAM needs more linear power.

figure.aria: A 4 by 4 grid of 16-QAM points at I and Q levels −3, −1, 1 and 3.

chapters.example: A 16-QAM system sends 20 Mbps over a 10 MHz null-to-null passband channel using rectangular pulses. Find the symbol rate, bits per symbol, and bandwidth efficiency. Does it fit? Answer: 16-QAM carries log2 16=4 bits per symbol. R_s=20 Mbps/4=5 Msym/s. B=2R_s=10 MHz. Efficiency=20 Mbps/10 MHz=2 bps/Hz. It fits exactly with zero excess bandwidth.
chapters.trap: Using M instead of log2 M for bits per symbol. QAM needs a linear amplifier and has a high peak-to-average power ratio. MFSK bandwidth grows with M; it is not a bandwidth-saving scheme.
chapters.prereq: 6.4 M-ary PSK; Unit 5 signal space and matched filter.
chapters.leave: MSK and GMSK to 6.6; OFDM use of QAM to 6.9; error-control coding to Unit 7.

chapters.idea: MSK is continuous-phase FSK with modulation index 0.5; GMSK filters the data first to shrink spectrum at the cost of ISI.
chapters.depth: Cover MSK: h=2Δf/R_b=0.5, constant envelope, continuous phase. Show the I/Q view as OQPSK with sinusoidal pulse weighting. Give generation by voltage-controlled oscillator or I/Q shaping, and coherent I/Q detection. State tone spacing 2Δf=R_b/2. Cover GMSK: a Gaussian lowpass filter before the MSK modulator, with BT product, where B is the Gaussian filter 3 dB bandwidth and T_b is bit duration. Smaller BT gives narrower spectrum but more ISI; BT=0.3 is a common value. Mention constant envelope for nonlinear amplifiers. Some syllabi call MSK fast FSK. Keep spectral plots qualitative.

figure.title: GMSK transmitter
figure.aria: Data passes through a Gaussian lowpass filter with BT=0.3, then an MSK modulator with h=0.5, producing GMSK.

chapters.example: A GMSK system has bit rate 270.833 kbps and BT=0.3. For MSK, h=0.5. Find the frequency deviation, tone spacing, and Gaussian filter 3 dB bandwidth. Answer: Δf=hR_b/2=0.5×270.833 kbps/2=67.708 kHz. Tone spacing=2Δf=135.416 kHz. Gaussian filter bandwidth B=BT/T_b=0.3×R_b=0.3×270.833 kHz=81.25 kHz.
chapters.trap: Using h=1 for MSK. MSK is not the same as ordinary BFSK; its phase is continuous. The GMSK filter reduces spectrum but adds ISI, so it does not increase the data rate by itself.
chapters.leave: GSM burst format and equalization to other subjects; OFDM to 6.9.

chapters.idea: Constellation distance sets error probability; constellation size sets bits per symbol and bandwidth efficiency.
chapters.depth: Review signal space from Unit 5: orthonormal basis, vector representation, decision regions. Define minimum Euclidean distance d_min and average symbol energy E_s. Show how d_min controls error probability and how M controls bits per symbol k=log2 M. Define bandwidth efficiency η=R_b/B bps/Hz. For rectangular null-to-null passband B≈2R_s, give η≈k/2; with ideal Nyquist passband B=R_s, give η≈k. Compare BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM and MFSK on the power-bandwidth plane. Mention Shannon limit only as a boundary, not a design formula. Keep union-bound derivation short.

figure.aria: BPSK points lie on the I axis, QPSK points sit at four corners, and 16-QAM points fill a 4 by 4 grid.

chapters.example: A 10 MHz passband channel uses rectangular pulses whose null-to-null bandwidth is B=2R_s. Find the maximum bit rate and bandwidth efficiency for BPSK, QPSK and 16-QAM. Answer: R_s=B/2=5 Msym/s. BPSK: R_b=5 Mbps, η=0.5 bps/Hz. QPSK: R_b=10 Mbps, η=1 bps/Hz. 16-QAM: R_b=20 Mbps, η=2 bps/Hz. All three use the same 10 MHz but need different Eb/N0 for the same P_b.
chapters.trap: Using baseband Nyquist bandwidth R_s/2 for a passband channel without doubling. Bandwidth efficiency is bits per second per hertz, not bits per symbol. Compare schemes at the same E_b, not the same E_s.
chapters.prereq: Unit 5 signal space; 6.2 BPSK; 6.4 QPSK; 6.5 QAM.
chapters.leave: Detailed error derivations to 6.2, 6.4 and 6.5; coding gain to Unit 7.

chapters.idea: Multiply a narrowband data signal by a fast pseudorandom code (DSSS) or hop its carrier (FHSS) so it occupies a wide band and resists interference.
chapters.depth: This chapter completes the subject: spread spectrum is a standard application of passband modulation. Cover PN sequences and chip rate R_c. Define processing gain G_p=R_c/R_b and give G_p in dB as 10 log10(R_c/R_b). Cover DSSS: data × PN code × carrier; receiver despreads with the same code, then demodulates. Cover jamming margin = G_p − required Eb/N0 in dB, with losses ignored. Cover FHSS: slow hopping and fast hopping, frequency synthesizer, and CDMA multiple access in one paragraph. Keep code acquisition and capacity analysis qualitative.

figure.title: DSSS transmitter and receiver
figure.aria: Data is multiplied by a PN code, BPSK modulated, sent through a channel, demodulated, multiplied again by the same PN code, integrated and thresholded.

chapters.example: A DSSS system has data rate 9.6 kbps and chip rate 1.2288 Mcps. Find the processing gain in dB. If the required Eb/N0 is 7 dB, find the jamming margin. Answer: G_p=1.2288×10⁶/9.6×10³=128. G_p=10 log10 128≈21.07 dB. Jamming margin≈21.07−7=14.07 dB.
chapters.trap: Confusing chip rate with bit rate. Add processing gain in dB, not linear. Despreading needs the same code and chip timing; a different code does not recover the data.
chapters.prereq: 6.2 BPSK; Unit 1 random processes and noise.
chapters.leave: Multi-user CDMA capacity to advanced courses; OFDM to 6.9.

chapters.idea: OFDM sends many orthogonal low-rate subcarriers via IFFT/FFT so a frequency-selective channel looks flat per subcarrier; a cyclic prefix absorbs delay spread.
chapters.depth: Cover OFDM: N subcarriers, subcarrier spacing Δf=1/T_u, useful symbol duration T_u, cyclic prefix T_cp, total symbol T=T_u+T_cp. Show transmitter IFFT and receiver FFT, one-tap equalizer per subcarrier, and orthogonality. State that the cyclic prefix must be longer than the channel delay spread. Mention PAPR and synchronisation as practical problems. Cover fading: flat versus frequency-selective, slow versus fast, coherence bandwidth and Doppler. Only a few universities teach the fading part; keep it short and qualitative. Mention OFDMA in LTE and Wi-Fi as an application.

figure.title: OFDM link
figure.aria: Data is QAM mapped, passed through an IFFT, cyclic prefix added, sent over a fading channel, cyclic prefix removed, FFT processed, QAM demapped and thresholded.

chapters.example: An OFDM system uses 64 subcarriers in 20 MHz, a 16-sample cyclic prefix, and 64-QAM on every subcarrier. Find the subcarrier spacing, useful symbol duration, cyclic prefix duration, total symbol duration, and uncoded bit rate. Answer: Δf=20 MHz/64=312.5 kHz. T_u=1/Δf=3.2 μs. Sample time=1/20 MHz=50 ns, so T_cp=16×50 ns=0.8 μs. T=3.2+0.8=4.0 μs. Bits per OFDM symbol=64×6=384. Bit rate=384/4.0 μs=96 Mbps.
chapters.trap: Forgetting cyclic prefix overhead in the data rate. OFDM does not remove fading; it turns frequency-selective fading into flat fading on each subcarrier. Do not confuse subcarrier spacing with symbol rate.
chapters.prereq: 6.4 QPSK; 6.5 QAM; Unit 5 ISI and Nyquist criterion; Unit 1 random processes.
chapters.leave: Detailed channel estimation, MIMO and PAPR reduction to advanced courses; error-control coding to Unit 7.
